title: Per-tenant private eval harness with encrypted golden bundles and rollup-only telemetry
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Goal: Provide every Dedicated/Private customer with an isolated eval harness that runs locally or within their VPC, consumes encrypted 'golden bundles' controlled by the customer, and emits only aggregate/rollup telemetry to Redwood's Console. This enables safe, repeatable regression detection tied to config or model changes while preserving tenant data sovereignty and minimizing shared-data leakage.
background: Customers running Redwood Dedicated and Private have asked for automated regression detection tied to config and model rollouts, but are restricted by data residency and compliance requirements. Current hosted eval pipelines are centralized and cannot be used as-is for many regulated customers. Earlier proposals (see PM-34122, PM-51234) explored shadow evals and local provenance; this ticket builds a production-ready, opt-in per-tenant eval runner that addresses cryptographic custody and telemetry minimization.
scope: MVP for this ticket: (1) encrypted golden bundle format and distribution mechanism, (2) a containerized eval runner that can execute locally or inside customer VPC (OCI image + Helm chart), (3) a rollup-only telemetry contract and Console UI placeholder to show pass/fail + trend without raw examples, (4) automatic gating integration to block model/config rollouts when regression exceeds thresholds. Out of scope: automatic creation of golden suites from customer corpora, multi-tenant shared golden deduplication (follow-on).
design_decisions: Use customer-held encryption keys (KMS/HSM) where available; Redwood supports envelope encryption but does not hold unencrypted goldens for Private installs.
Eval runner runs as a Kubernetes job or a managed container in VPC with no egress by default; only encrypted rollups (counts, metrics, masked deltas) are permitted to leave the environment.
We will support a signed 'golden bundle' format (.rwgold) with manifest, hash, and signature to enable provenance checks during ingestion.
Gating thresholds are configurable per-customer and can be tied to existing rollout policies (canary, A/B, automatic rollback).
Telemetry uses delta metrics with l1 clipping and quantization to minimize leakage; raw prompts/responses are never transmitted.
To save storage, customers may reference shared read-only blobs by checksum; Redwood will provide tooling to locally fetch and validate these when customer permits.
Default retention for local eval artifacts is 90 days; configurable by customer to meet compliance needs.
tradeoffs: Per-tenant execution increases CPU/GPU overhead and storage duplication versus centralized host-based evals; mitigated by recommending smaller sample sizes for frequent checks and full suites on scheduled cadence.

Client-side-only telemetry reduces our ability to debug subtle regressions; mitigation: provide an 'opt-in debug' flow where customers can temporarily grant Redwood access to ephemeral encrypted artifacts under strict audit rules.
Using customer KMS adds operational complexity for onboarding and key rotation; but is necessary for compliance-sensitive customers.
Encrypted golden bundles complicate fast cross-customer comparisons; recommend internal tooling for customers to export standardized metrics for cross-tenant benchmarking when allowed.
Blocking rollouts conservatively may increase incident response churn for SRE; plan to provide a 'soft-block' mode that only notifies for the first two occurrences before enforcing.
We will defer implementing differential privacy mechanisms for now to reduce scope; rollup-only telemetry is lower-risk short-term compromise.

acceptance_criteria: Provisioned eval runner OCI image and Helm chart that can be deployed into a customer private cluster with documented inputs
Encrypted golden bundle spec and tooling to create/sign/verify bundles (CLI) available
Console shows per-tenant rollup metrics with pass/fail and 14d trend; raw example text is never displayed or stored centrally
Gating integration present: when regression metric exceeds tenant-configured threshold, the rollout API blocks the change and emits a clear actionable reason
Security review completed and checklist items addressed (KMS integration, no-raw-data-exfiltration, audit logs)
Pilot customers (>=2) approve the telemetry contract and report no compliance blockers
implementation_notes: Engineering will reuse existing evaluation harness code where possible (ENG-87420) and implement the golden bundle verifier as a library in rust/go for portability. Ops will publish a hardened minimal image and helm templates. Product will prepare onboarding guide and telemetry contract language for legal/compliance.
risks: Customers may have strict network policies that prevent bundle fetch; need offline bundle delivery process
Onboarding complexity could slow adoption; mitigate with a managed onboarding playbook and SRE runbook
If rollup metrics are insufficient to explain regressions, customers may request temporary access to raw data which increases compliance risk
open_questions: Do we require Redwood to provide a signed bundle registry for customers that cannot host their own bundles? (security/legal implications)
Should soft-block mode allow automatic retry with a smaller evaluation sample before final rollback?
What is the canonical set of metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity/LL-perplexity/custom-tests) we surface in rollups by default?
